## The Core Claim

A strategy can be evolutionarily stable -- resistant to invasion by any alternative strategy -- without any player consciously choosing it or reasoning strategically at all; stability emerges from differential reproductive success alone, and an evolutionarily stable strategy (Maynard Smith & Price, 1973) is provably a Nash equilibrium of the corresponding game. Nash won the 1994 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for equilibrium analysis in non-cooperative games, the same formal object evolutionary game theory later showed applies without conscious agents at all.
